building.name: Fresno Building Code: the California Building Code (Title 24, Part 2) as adopted by Fresno Municipal Code section 11-101 with the local amendments in section 11-102
building.effective: 2026-01-01 (the 2025 state code). The city's adopting ordinance, Bill B-40, was passed by the City Council on 2025-09-25 and takes effect on the thirty-first day after final passage.
building.quote: SECTION 11-101. CALIFORNIA BUILDING CODE. The California Building Code. 2025 Edition, which may be referred to in this Code as the CBC, as promulgated by the California Building Standards Commission, which incorporates the adoption of the 2024 edition of the of the International Building Code as amended with necessary California amendments and the 2024 International Building Code of the International Code Council with the exception of Appendix B, are adopted and incorporated by reference into the Municipal Code and shall be referred to, along with the City's amendments to the CBC provided in section 11-102, as the Fresno Building Code.

other_quotes.quote: BILL B-40 (Introduced September 11, 2025)(For Adoption) Repealing and Replacing Sections 11-101 Through 11-109 of Article 1, Chapter 11 of the Fresno Municipal Code, relating to the Adoption and Amendment of the 2025 Edition of the California Building Standards Code (Subject to Mayor's Veto) ... 25-1252 · Action Item · Passed ... Thu, Sep 25, 2025 City Council APPROVED ON CONSENT CALENDAR Pass

The 2025 California Building Standards Code will become effective on January 1, 2026, and is mandated by the California Building Standards Commission for statewide adoption and enforcement. ... Regardless of whether the City formally adopts the California Building Standards Code it will go into effect on January 1, 2026.
SECTION 5. This ordinance shall become effective and in full force and effect at 12:01 a.m. on the thirty-first day after its final passage.

building.note: The city's building code amendments (section 11-102) are: Chapter 1 sections 103.1, 104.1, 109.2, 109.5, 110.3.8, 112.1, 112.2, 112.2.1, 113.1, 113.2.1 and 114.4.1 (enforcing agency, fees, inspections, utility connections, appeals board, violations), cross-reference notes to the Fresno Fire Code at Chapter 9 and section 1024, and section 1208.4 (efficiency dwelling units). None touches toilet rooms or interior finishes, and section 105.2 (work exempt from permit) is not amended. The ordinance text read is the unsigned copy attached to the council item (a scan, read by OCR); the ordinance number and the signed dates were not read.

plumbing.name: Fresno Plumbing Code: the California Plumbing Code (Title 24, Part 5) as adopted by Fresno Municipal Code section 11-107 with the local amendment in section 11-107A
plumbing.effective: 2026-01-01 (the 2025 state code; same ordinance, Bill B-40, passed 2025-09-25)
plumbing.quote: SECTION 11-107. CALIFORNIA PLUMBING CODE. The California Plumbing Code, 2025 Edition, which may be referred to in the Code as the CPC, as promulgated by the California Building Standards Commission, which incorporates the adoption of the 2024 edition of the Uniform Plumbing Code as amended with necessary California amendments and the 2024 Uniform Plumbing Code of the International Association of Plumbing and Mechanical Officials, is hereby adopted by the City of Fresno and incorporated by reference into the Fresno Building Code

other_quotes.quote: SECTION 11-107A. AMENDMENTS TO CALIFORNIA PLUMBING CODE. ... CPC Chapter 6 604.0 Materials 604.1 Pipe, Tube, and Fittings. The third paragraph of section 604.1 of the California Plumbing Code is hereby deleted in its entirety and amended to read: Materials for building water piping and building supply piping shall be in accordance with the applicable standards referenced in Table 604.1. Galvanized malleable iron, galvanized wrought iron or galvanized steel are prohibited materials for use both underground and in buildings.

plumbing.note: The only plumbing amendment bans galvanized iron and steel water pipe. Chapter 4 (fixtures) is not amended.

fixtures.text: Fresno adopts the 2025 California Plumbing Code and amends only the third paragraph of section 604.1 (pipe materials; Fresno Municipal Code section 11-107A). Section 422 and Table 422.1 are untouched, so the state's counts and the state pack's worked examples stand. The council staff report names the same single plumbing amendment. No city bulletin or handout on fixture counts is listed on the Building and Safety pages.
fixtures.quote: The proposed modification to the California Plumbing Code requires express findings and is related to the prohibition of galvanized malleable iron, galvanized wrought iron or galvanized steel for building water piping and building supply piping.
fixtures.worked_examples_note: Not redone: the table is the state's, so the state pack's rows apply. The statements used in the page text (50/50 split, urinals, women's count, single restroom for offices and shops of 50 or fewer, new buildings, additions and changes of use, floor area per person) come from the 2025 California Plumbing Code as read for the California pack and the Sacramento page, not from a Fresno document.

permit.exempt_list_quote: [A] 105.2 Work Exempt From Permit. Exemptions from permit requirements of this code shall not be deemed to grant authorization for any work to be done in any manner in violation of the provisions of this code or any other laws or ordinances of this jurisdiction. Permits shall not be required for the following: Building: One-story detached accessory structures used as tool and storage sheds, playhouses and similar uses, provided that the floor area does not exceed than 120 square feet. ... Fences, other than swimming pool barriers, not over 7 feet high. Oil derricks. Retaining walls that are not over 4 feet in height ... Water tanks supported directly on grade if the capacity is not greater than 5,000 gallons ... Sidewalks and driveways not more than 30 inches above adjacent grade, and not over any basement or story below and are not part of an accessible route. Painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, countertops and similar finish work. Temporary motion picture, television and theater stage sets and scenery. Prefabricated swimming pools accessory to a Group R-3 occupancy ... Shade cloth structures constructed for nursery or agricultural purposes, not including service systems. Swings and other playground equipment accessory to detached one- and two-family dwellings. Window awnings in Group R-3 and U occupancies ... Nonfixed and movable fixtures, cases, racks, counters and partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches (1753 mm) in height.
permit.exempt_list_note: Fresno publishes no exempt-work list of its own. Its ordinance adopts the state building code's Chapter 1 and does not amend section 105.2, so the state list applies. That list was read on UpCodes (2025 California Building Code, Chapter 1, Division II), a secondary copy.
permit.rule_quote: Chapter 1, section 105.1 of the California Building Code (CBC) states: "Any owner or authorized agent who intends to construct, alter, repair, move, demolish, or change the occupancy of a building or structure, or to erect, install, enlarge, alter, repair, remove, convert or replace any electrical, gas, mechanical or plumbing system shall obtain the required permit."
permit.partitions_note: The state list exempts 'nonfixed and movable ... partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches' without naming toilet partitions or saying whether floor-anchored or overhead-braced compartments count. The question is left open here.
permit.office: City of Fresno Planning and Development Department, Building and Safety Services Division (Fresno City Hall, 2600 Fresno Street, Third Floor)
permit.phone_quote: Additional Information Building Permits: 559.621.8084 Inspection Services: 559.621.8116
permit.confidence: high for the city's rule and phone number; medium for the state list (secondary copy)

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Fresno job sites. Price your restroom in five questions and see the California and city rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Fresno schools, hospitals, packing houses and distribution centers, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Fresno uses California's rules, which set the number of toilets and urinals by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Fresno follows California's permit rules: a permit is needed to "construct, alter, repair" a building, and the city hasn't changed the state's list of work that needs none. That list covers "painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, countertops and similar finish work" and movable "partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches" high. It doesn't name toilet partitions, so ask Building and Safety (559-621-8084) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: City of Fresno Building and Safety
page.stalls_intro: Fresno counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women, and California's rules require urinals in the men's room. Every toilet needs a stall, and urinals need screens between them. The women's room must have at least as many toilets as the men's room has toilets and urinals together.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for new buildings, additions and changes of use that bring in more people. An office or shop with 50 people or fewer may have a single one-person restroom. At least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, California's plumbing rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, and a restaurant dining room or a classroom at one per 30 square feet. Your architect or City of Fresno Building and Safety sets the final number.
page.install_rule: In Fresno, a business working in the city needs a City of Fresno Business Tax Certificate, and building permits come from Building and Safety. California requires its contractor license, usually the C-61/D-34 class, for partition installs of $1,000 or more, and at any price when the job needs workers or a permit. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: In Fresno the contractor needs a California contractor license for jobs of $1,000 or more and a city Business Tax Certificate.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** California requires the state-set wage on public jobs over $1,000, including city and school district work. For a carpenter in Fresno County that is $67.23 an hour plus $34.95 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 8.35% in Fresno: 7.25% statewide, 0.725% in three county taxes (transportation, libraries and the zoo) and 0.375% city.
page.buyers_extra: - **Packing houses and food processors:** solid plastic (HDPE) or stainless steel for restrooms that are washed down every day.
